issues.description: The Developer initializer parameter type is inconsistent across artifacts: the problem statement and the template expect monthsOfSwiftExperience to be provided as an optional (Int?), but the solution's Developer initializer uses a non-optional Int parameter. This mismatch can confuse students about the intended constructor signature and which values (including nil) are allowed when creating a Developer.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's Developer initializer accept an optional Int (monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) to match the problem specification and the template, and update the implementation to handle nil appropriately (e.g., assign directly to the optional property and print the description).

issues.description: Within the solution repository, the Developer initializer signature (monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int) conflicts with how Developer is instantiated in Client.swift (passing nil). This internal inconsistency causes a compile-time error and indicates the solution code is not self-consistent.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Developer initializer in the solution accept an optional Int (monthsOfSwiftExperience: Int?) so the call Developer(name: "Your Name", monthsOfSwiftExperience: nil) compiles, or alternatively change the Client instantiation to pass a non-nil Int for all Developer instances. Prefer aligning the initializer with the problem statement (use Int?).
